section.content: I began my academic journey at Carleton University in Ottawa, receiving a BSc in biochemistry in 2020. I had a fantastic experience at Carleton, meeting many wonderful people. My experience in the biochemistry program gave me the mathematical, scientific, and analytical foundations that continue to benefit me in both my academic and professional careers to this day.
section.content2: Following my biochemistry degree, I pursued a BCS in Computer Science at Carleton, graduating in 2022, using my computer science credits from the biochemistry degree to fast-track my studies. During my time in the computer science program, I developed a passion for software development and problem-solving, which has driven me to continue learning and growing in this field.
section.content3: After graduating from Carleton with a BCS in Computer Science and working for a year, I pursued further studies at the Université de Bordeaux in France, as a recipient of the Graduate Studies in France scholarship from the French government.
section.content4: Studying in France was a lifechanging experience that markedly improved my social skills, my French and Spanish language skills, and broadened my knowledge of the world around me. Inside the classroom, this included learning about marketing and project management, while outside the classroom, I developed a deeper appreciation for different cultures and ways of life, including an appreciation for Bordelais wine and French cheeses.
section.content5: I have a deep appreciation for all the educators, mentors, and peers who have supported me throughout my time in academia. You have all played a significant role in shaping my path in life, and I am grateful for the knowledge and experiences that I have gained along the way!

section.content: Recently, I have begun to experiment with making YouTube videos, with a focus on historical and cultural content. I use Kdenlive as my video editor, which I highly recommend as a piece of free and open-source software.
section.content2: For my MBA program, I wrote two significant papers. The first was a market analysis of the online dating industry, highlighting how the existing dating app business model is adverse to the user, and a proposal for a new entrant into the market.
section.content3: The second paper was detailed analysis of the tariff policy of the Trump administration, as of August 2021, looking at White House statements and press releases and examining the potential economic impacts of the tariffs on both the US and global economies. This included a comparison to three historical instances of tariff implementations or political economic accords, and their economic effects; the Smoot-Hawley Tariff Act of 1930, the Abominable Tariff of 1828, and the Plaza Accord of 1985.

section.content: Previously, I worked as a software developer for Dell Technologies, developing a testing framework for their 5G infrastructure products. This role significantly enhanced my skills in Python and exposed me to test automation, CI/CD pipelines, and telecommunications technologies.
section.content2: Prior to Dell, I worked with the DDR PHY team at Synopsys as a DDR PHY Engineering Intern, where I contributed to the design and verification of high-speed memory interfaces. This experience was invaluable to me, as it provided a fantastic understanding of the interaction between hardware and software; many features of higher level programming languages are the direct result of hardware capabilities.
section.content3: During the COVID-19 pandemic, I had the privilege of interning with the Government of Canada's COVID-19 Task Force. This was my first exposure to public sector work, at a very interesting time. I reviewed over $10 million in grant applications related to COVID-19, and successfully collated, cleaned, and analyzed rapid antigen testing data from pharmacies and small business across Canada.

section.content: My name is Carson! I am currently a US-based consultant in the financial technology sector. My passions include history, hiking, economics, web development, numismatics, sport shooting, and going on adventures.
section.content2: Previously, I lived for several months in Türkiye, where I learned extensively about Turkish, Ottoman, and Byzantine history, and traveled extensively throughout the country. The best food is the iskender kebab! It's kebab, tomato sauce and pita drizzled in brown butter and served with Greek yogurt. I ate it everywhere, including the restaurant that invented it in Bursa. Highly recommended!
section.content3: I also had the pleasure of living in Bordeaux, France for two years during my Master's studies. France is a wonderful country and Bordeaux, a wonderful city. The southwestern region of France is less explored by tourists, but has so much to offer in terms of history, culture, food, and wine.
section.content4: In my free time, I enjoy going on extended hikes and enjoying my love for the outdoors. This includes doing the Camino de Santiago in Spain, the Ruta Vicentina in Portugal, and various other trails across North America and Europe.
section.content5: I am also an avid history enthusiast, with a particular interest in economic, political and military history. I am a member of various numismatic clubs and organizations and enjoy collecting historical coins and artifacts from around the world. My particular areas of interest include Hellenistic Era, Rome, the Byzantine Empire, the Age of Revolutions, and early modern European history.
section.content6: When I develop web applications, my stack of choice includes Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, and Node.js. I enjoy building both front-end and back-end solutions. For non-web development projects, I often use Python for data analysis and automation tasks.
section.content7: I am always eager to meet likeminded people and seek out new opportunities, so feel free to reach out!

01-25-2026.title: Europe must concede nothing to the Trump Administration, for its own sake.

content.paragraph1: In January 2026, US President Donald J. Trump announced, on Truth Social, that the United States would be implementing a blanket 10% tariff on all imports from select European countries (Denmark, Norway, Sweden, France, Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and Finland), starting February 1st, 2026, in response to Danish refusal to give up sovereignty over Greenland. President Trump has repeatedly stated that American national security is at risk if Greenland is not under US control, and threatened to raise tariffs to 25% if Denmark does not comply.
content.paragraph2: First of all, one must address the sheer ridiculousness of the notion that the United States "needs" Greenland for national security reasons. Thus far, American reasoning for wanting the territory largely falls within two main lines of reasoning: the first, being that there is an imminent threat that China or Russia will use opening Arctic waterways to gain strategic leverage over the United States, and that the US needs a greater military presence in Greenland to counter this threat; the second, is that Greenland is rich in rare earth minerals, which are necessary for the production of modern technology, such as solar panels and military hardware.
content.paragraph3: These claims are dubious at best; the US already has a base on Greenland, and the 1951 Greenland Defense Agreement gives the US wide breadth to expand its presence on the island if it were to so choose.
content.paragraph4: As for rare earth minerals, Greenland does have significant deposits. However, Greenland only ranks 8th worldwide for confirmed deposits of rare earth minerals... behind the United States itself. Exploratory drilling is also merely an estimate of deposits, and does not mean it is economically viable to extract them. Finally, despite their name, rare earth minerals are actually relatively abundant in the Earth's crust; the issue is that they are found in small concentrations in other ores, and require significant processing to extract.
content.paragraph5: However, let us put aside, for the moment, all of that. The notion that the US requires Greenland for "national security" is farcical. I would also be militarily and economically safer if I owned Greenland. I would also be safer if I owned Iceland, and the United States, even the entire planet. But alas, we live in a world of other human beings, and need to learn to share resources like adults.
content.paragraph6: Alas, President Trump has since posted, on January 21st, again on Truth Social, that a "framework of a future deal" had been reached with Mark Rutte, the current Secretary General of NATO. While details remain fuzzy, Trump has stated that:
content.paragraph7: The time limit is infinity, meaning there is no time limit. It's forever. You know, you're about 99 years, 50 years. It's forever. That was discussed. We can do anything we want. We can do military, we can do anything we want, and it's being negotiated. And let's see what happens. I think it'll be good.
content.paragraph8: Implying that Denmark will, in fact, concede some territory to the United States. While this seems like a trivial concession to make a potentially disastrous diplomatic row go away, Europe is making a grave mistake by making any concessions to the Trump administration.
content.paragraph9: By allowing the Americans to threaten and bully their way to any sort of shift in the status quo, particularly one that involves conceding territory, Europe is proving to President Trump and his supporters that such tactics are effective. By choosing to cede even the smallest amount of territory, Trump supporters believe that the President is a master negotiator, a savvy businessman who garners concessions without firing a shot, by choosing to anchor negotiations at an extreme position, and then working backwards to gain a favorable outcome.
content.paragraph10: President Trump, for all his bluster and unpredictability, does respect strength. He has repeatedly expressed respect for President Xi of China and President Putin of Russia, and disrespected pliable leaders such as Rutte (whose mandate is now, admittedly, maintaining NATO, even if it's too the detriment of the majority of its members, including the Netherlands, of which he is a former Prime Minister). By refusing to concede anything to the Trump administration, Europe will be sending a clear message that such tactics will not work, and that the United States must engage in good faith negotiations, rather than trying to bully its way to favorable outcomes.
content.paragraph11: The Greenland Crisis, while still treated as a sideshow in the United States, represents an existential threat to NATO, Canada (whom Trump has already expressed interest in annexing, and would be surrounded on three sides if an American Greenland were to come to pass), and possibly some EU countries themselves. While Europe remains divided, there is hope that facing such a grave threat to their sovereignty will bring urgency for the Europeans to work together, and perhaps, just maybe, federate.
content.paragraph12: Even if this commentary seems politically charged, this is as much game theory as it is geopolitics. The Trump administration's style of negotiation is akin to brinksmanship, and they do it much better than the previous Biden administration.
content.paragraph13: While the hour is dark for the west, we come from a rich heritage of free thinkers, who have adapted and adopted to political systems and ideals when the old ways no longer served us. What the numbers do not show, is a Europe that is stronger and richer than it thinks; with a robust manufacturing base, a strong agricultural sector, innovative tech hubs, capable militaries, and an unmatched cultural heritage. The numbers don't tell the whole story, with a United States that increasingly sells financial services and vaporware that provide an illusion of prosperity where there is less and less to be found. With some encouragement and bravery, it is possible for the rest of the west to come together and find a new path forward, one that does not involve kowtowing to whichever autocrat feels like throwing around their weight that day.
